newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SUNDERLAND FIGHT BACK TO GAIN DRAW AGAINST MIDDLESBROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUNDERLAND FIGHT BACK TO GAIN DRAW AGAINST MIDDLESBROUGH.

text.p: Sunderland fought back to earn a 2-2 draw despite being reduced to 10 men early in the second half of their northern derby against Middlesborough on Monday.
Fabrizio Ravanelli fired Middlesbrough into a 2-1 lead eight minutes into the second-half with his 11th goal of the season and his first away from home.
When Richard Ord was sent off for stamping on Nick Barmby five minutes later Sunderland had a mountain to climb.
But Peter Reid's men refused to give up the fight and substitute Craig Russell earned them a 61st-minute equaliser.

Brazilian Emerson had given Middlesbrough an 18th-minute lead with a spectacular 25-yard strike but Alex Rae equalised from the penalty spot four minutes later after Phil Whelan had fouled Paul Stewart.
Ord's dismissal was Sunderland's third in their last two games following the sending off of Martin Scott and Stewart at Arsenal, although Stewart was later cleared by referee Paul Danson.
